what_it_does: Cloud providers need to charge tenants fairly for their carbon emissions from running AI workloads. Today's billing methods assume fixed overhead per hour, but in reality, a machine's embodied carbon (emissions from manufacturing it) gets amortized only across actual utilization—high-demand periods amortize more carbon cost, low-demand periods amortize less. Also, when workloads run on the same machine, they interfere with each other, degrading performance and wasting energy. Fair-CO2 uses game theory (Shapley value) to fairly split shared costs: it adjusts hardware depreciation based on real-time utilization and accounts for interference between colocated workloads. Since exact computation is too slow, it uses tractable approximations validated with simulation.
